# Overview of the EHRSQL 2024 Shared Task on Reliable Text-to-SQL Modeling on Electronic Health Records

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#ehrsql-2024)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2024.clinicalnlp-1.62.pdf) · ClinicalNLP 2024 proceedings, printed pages 644–654

**Reading coverage:** All 11 pages: sections 1–6, limitations, figures 1–2, tables 1–3, references and Appendix A fact-sheet template.

## Research question

Clinical database QA must reject unsupported questions and incorrect SQL instead of optimizing answerable-only generation accuracy.

## Method

The shared task adapts EHRSQL templates to MIMIC-IV Demo, regenerates paraphrases with manual checking, adds TrustSQL-derived negatives and reserves unseen question templates for validation/test.

## Evaluation

Eight teams are compared using execution-based Reliability Score. Correct answers and correct refusals earn one; abstaining on answerable questions earns zero; wrong answers or answering unsupported questions incur a configurable penalty. The principal ranking uses penalty 10; an abstain-all baseline scores about 20 on evaluation splits.

## What the results support

Unified LLM methods lead this particular leaderboard. Every submitted system loses to abstain-all under the most severe penalty, illustrating that high moderate-penalty scores still allow errors. This comparison does not isolate architecture from model strength, training or ensembling.

## Limits and qualifications

Data cover a 100-patient demo schema and selected question templates; preprocessing removes duplicate values to reduce ambiguity. Table 1 gives 450 negatives among 5,124 training samples, about 8.8%, compared with approximately 20% in validation and test.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A useful clinical abstention protocol whose denominator, penalty and schema preprocessing must accompany reported reliability.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Unanswerable-question prevalence is equal across all splits. | Table 1 lists training 450/5124, validation 232/1163 and test 233/1167. Section 3.5 discusses adding new unanswerable questions exclusively to validation and test before describing their 20% proportions. | Section 3.5 and Table 1, printed page 647 | Use the split-specific counts; the 20% description applies to evaluation splits. |
| Winning systems are reliable under all penalties. | Table 3 shows negative RS_N for every team versus abstain-all 20.0. | Sections 4.1, 4.3; Table 3, printed page 649 | Not supported; conclusions must specify the selected error penalty. |
